article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Sativa / 30% Indica
Genetics: Clementine × Pre-98 Bubba Kush
Breeder: World Breeders / The Cali Connection
THC Content: 26–28%
CBD Content: 0.1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Clementine, mandarin orange, citrus peel
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September / early October
Indoor Yield: 300–900+ g/m²
Outdoor Yield: High potential
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Imagine cutting into a perfectly ripe clementine while a jar of old-school Kush sits open nearby, and the unusual character of Clementine Slush begins to make sense. Rather than pursuing the candy-heavy direction common to many modern marijuana hybrids, this strain puts bright citrus against darker notes of roasted coffee, earth, chocolate, and hash.

Its breeding also creates an interesting contradiction: the plant grows with considerable vigor and branching, yet its flowering cycle can finish surprisingly quickly for a cultivar with pronounced sativa influence. Potency is another defining feature, with breeder figures placing THC in the upper-20-percent range. The result is weed aimed primarily at experienced consumers and growers who appreciate powerful effects, assertive terpene expression, heavy resin coverage, and genetics that combine contemporary citrus character with the deeper personality of classic Bubba Kush .
Genetics and Lineage

Clementine Slush was developed as a collaboration between World Breeders and The Cali Connection. The documented cross uses a selected World Breeders Clementine phenotype as the female side and The Cali Connection’s Pre-98 Bubba Kush in reversed form as the pollen donor. That distinction matters because several conflicting genetic descriptions circulate for this cultivar. The collaboration itself identifies the foundation as WB Clementine × Pre-98 Bubba Kush, with the Clementine selection tracing its citrus-heavy character back toward Tangie -related genetics. World Breeders classifies the resulting plant at approximately 70% sativa and 30% indica, which fits the vigorous growth, extensive lateral branching, and lively cerebral qualities associated with the finished hybrid.

Clementine’s ancestry supplies much of the brighter side of the cross. Clementine was originally developed from Tangie-related citrus genetics and is associated with sharp mandarin, orange zest, sweetness, energetic growth, and an upbeat psychoactive profile. Tangie itself descends from California Orange and Skunk -family genetics, giving this branch of the family tree a long connection to unmistakable orange aromas. Such traits can be particularly dominant during vegetative growth and early flowering, when citrus-oriented plants often stretch rapidly and create numerous secondary branches rather than concentrating all of their production around a single central stalk.

Pre-98 Bubba Kush pulls the offspring in a very different direction. This famous old-school Kush variety is treasured for dense flowers, exceptional resin, earthy hash aromas, coffee and cocoa nuances, and a distinctly relaxing physical quality. It also contributes a relatively compact flowering cycle compared with many citrus-heavy sativa lines. Bringing the two parents together therefore does more than combine orange and Kush flavors. The Bubba influence helps shorten flowering, deepen the resin output, strengthen the darker aromatic base, and add physical calm to what might otherwise be an intensely stimulating Clementine expression.
Effects and Experience

The first phase generally favors the Clementine side of the family. A moderate amount can produce a noticeable change in mental tempo, with thoughts feeling quicker, conversation becoming easier, and routine activities taking on greater novelty. Rather than beginning with immediate heaviness, the experience often develops above the shoulders first. Mood elevation, creative thinking, sensory appreciation, and an inclination toward activity fit naturally with the sativa-dominant pedigree. Music, outdoor recreation, creative hobbies, casual social settings, and other activities that benefit from an engaged state of mind may pair especially well with the cultivar.

As the session develops, Pre-98 Bubba Kush begins to become more apparent. The transition is less like switching from stimulation to sedation and more like gradually adding physical weight underneath an alert mental state. Muscles may loosen, bodily tension can become less noticeable, and the initially energetic character often becomes calmer and more settled. This progression helps distinguish Clementine Slush from marijuana varieties that stay relentlessly cerebral from beginning to end. Smaller servings may remain functional and socially oriented, while heavier consumption is more likely to reveal the Kush side and encourage quiet relaxation.

Potency deserves particular attention. With breeder specifications around 26–28% THC, this is not especially forgiving weed for inexperienced consumers. A large inhaled dose can turn an appealing mental lift into racing thoughts, dizziness, impaired coordination, or anxiety in THC-sensitive individuals. Starting low is particularly sensible with unfamiliar flower because cultivation, phenotype, curing, storage, and laboratory methodology can all influence cannabinoid concentration. Experienced consumers may appreciate the cultivar’s combination of intensity and dimensionality, but the same strength that gives it recreational appeal also makes dosage discipline important.
Medical Benefits

Clementine Slush has not been established through clinical trials as a treatment for any specific medical condition, so its potential therapeutic value is better understood through its cannabinoid profile and the kinds of experiences commonly associated with high-THC cannabis. The early uplifting portion may appeal to medical marijuana patients seeking temporary relief from low mood, stress, mental fatigue, or difficulty unwinding. Because its psychoactive effects can remain comparatively engaging at modest amounts, some consumers may prefer it during periods when they want relaxation without immediately becoming sleepy or disengaged.

Later in the experience, its Bubba Kush heritage may make the cultivar more relevant for physical discomfort. Relaxation, reduced perception of tension, and the distracting quality of a strong cannabis effect can be useful to some adults dealing with aches or general discomfort. Appetite stimulation may also occur, particularly as the initial energetic phase fades. These possibilities should not be interpreted as proof that the strain treats pain, anxiety, depression , appetite disorders, or other medical conditions. Cannabis responses differ widely, and THC can worsen anxiety or produce unwanted cognitive effects in susceptible individuals.

The very low CBD content is another important consideration. Clementine Slush is fundamentally a THC-dominant cannabis strain rather than a balanced medical marijuana variety. Patients who specifically benefit from substantial CBD will probably need a different chemotype or an additional CBD product. Anyone using prescription medication, managing cardiovascular or psychiatric conditions, preparing for surgery, pregnant or breastfeeding, or otherwise facing a significant medical issue should discuss cannabis use with a qualified healthcare professional rather than relying on a strain description as medical guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fresh citrus drives the aromatic introduction, but calling Clementine Slush simply an orange-flavored strain misses much of what gives it identity. Breaking apart properly cured flowers can release an immediate rush reminiscent of clementine peel, mandarin oil, sweet orange rind, and concentrated citrus zest. The brightness has a penetrating quality rather than the soft fruitiness of many dessert hybrids. Limonene is the terpene most consistent with this expression, although the exact terpene percentages can vary by phenotype and cultivation environment rather than following one universal laboratory profile.

Once the initial citrus impression settles, an entirely different layer becomes easier to identify. Earth, dark roast coffee, cocoa, hash oil, wood, and light spice can appear underneath the fruit. Those notes connect strongly to the Pre-98 Bubba Kush side and give the aroma a deeper finish than Clementine alone would normally provide. The contrast can resemble orange peel beside freshly ground coffee or citrus oil over an earthy hash base. Depending on the individual plant, subtle pepper, pine, floral, or herbal accents may emerge as well, reflecting secondary terpenes such as caryophyllene, myrcene, pinene, or related compounds.

Flavor tends to follow the aroma but changes through the inhale and exhale. The initial draw emphasizes juicy mandarin and sweet citrus before transitioning toward earthy Kush, roasted coffee, chocolate, and resinous hash. Vaporization at controlled temperatures can preserve more of the volatile citrus character, whereas combustion tends to emphasize the heavier roasted and hash-like notes. A slow, careful cure is especially valuable with this cultivar because overdrying can flatten the top-end citrus aroma and leave the heavier Kush elements disproportionately dominant.
Growing Information

Cultivators should prepare for more vegetative ambition than the relatively short flowering period might suggest. Clementine Slush grows quickly and produces extensive lateral branching, with The Cali Connection describing a naturally pine-tree-like structure. Left untouched, a healthy plant can develop numerous upward-reaching side branches capable of forming substantial colas. That architecture makes low-stress training particularly useful indoors. Bending and spreading the canopy early can prevent one portion of the plant from dominating the available light while turning its natural branching habit into a broad, productive flowering surface.

Indoor flowering generally requires about eight to nine weeks, unusually convenient for a plant carrying this much sativa character. Stretch should still be anticipated before the light cycle is changed because vigorous specimens can use vertical space rapidly. Strategic pruning of weak interior growth improves air circulation and redirects resources toward productive branches, but excessive stripping can work against the cultivar’s naturally strong side-cola development. Support may become worthwhile late in bloom as flowers accumulate mass and resin. The breeder describes exceptionally heavy trichome production and reports strong wash potential for solventless extraction, another reason to handle mature flowers carefully.

Outdoor gardens offer the plant room to express its larger structure, provided the climate supplies abundant sun and a reasonably dry finishing period. In the Northern Hemisphere, growers can generally anticipate harvest around late September into early October depending on latitude, phenotype, planting date, and seasonal weather. The shortened flowering influence from Pre-98 Bubba Kush can be an advantage in regions where autumn rain arrives relatively early. Even so, dense resinous flowers require good airflow and regular inspection during humid weather. Properly managed plants can deliver medium-to-high or potentially very large harvests, but environment matters far more than headline yield figures. Strong light, adequate root volume, disciplined irrigation, balanced nutrition, structural training, and careful drying ultimately determine how much of the cultivar’s genetic potential reaches the jar.
FAQ
Is Clementine Slush indica or sativa?

Clementine Slush is a sativa-dominant hybrid. World Breeders lists it at approximately 70% sativa and 30% indica. Its Clementine heritage contributes vigorous growth and an uplifting cerebral character, while Pre-98 Bubba Kush adds denser flower traits, physical relaxation, resin production, and a faster finish than might normally be expected from strongly citrus-oriented sativa genetics.
What are the genetics of Clementine Slush?

The breeder collaboration identifies the cross as a World Breeders Select Clementine phenotype × The Cali Connection Pre-98 Bubba Kush reversed male. The Clementine side is connected to Tangie-derived citrus genetics, while Pre-98 Bubba Kush represents the classic earthy, coffee-like Kush side of the family. Together they create a cultivar combining bright fruit terpenes with darker hash and roasted flavors.
How strong is Clementine Slush?

World Breeders lists THC at approximately 26–28% and CBD around 0.1%, placing the cultivar firmly in the high-potency category. Actual laboratory results can vary according to phenotype and growing conditions. Because of that THC concentration, inexperienced consumers should approach the weed conservatively rather than treating it as an average-strength hybrid.
What does Clementine Slush taste like?

The most recognizable flavor is sweet mandarin and clementine citrus, often accompanied by orange peel and tart citrus oil. Underneath the fruit are contrasting notes of earth, coffee, chocolate, spice, and hash. The combination is one of the strain’s most distinctive characteristics because neither genetic side completely overwhelms the other.
How long does Clementine Slush take to flower?

Indoor plants generally finish in approximately eight to nine weeks of flowering. That comparatively quick schedule is notable because the cultivar retains vigorous, sativa-influenced growth. Outdoors, harvest commonly falls around late September through early October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, although latitude and weather can shift the schedule.
Final Thoughts on Clementine Slush

Clementine Slush succeeds by putting two very different cannabis traditions into the same plant without erasing either one. Clementine contributes the penetrating mandarin aroma, rapid branching, energetic mental character, and unmistakable West Coast citrus influence. Pre-98 Bubba Kush supplies the counterweight: coffee, chocolate, earth, hash, dense resin, physical ease, and a shortened flowering period. The resulting marijuana hybrid can begin bright and lively before gradually settling into something heavier and more relaxed, while its flavor moves through an equally broad spectrum from fresh citrus peel to roasted Kush.

For growers, the main attractions are vigorous branching, abundant trichome production, substantial yield potential, and an eight-to-nine-week flowering period that is relatively manageable for sativa-dominant genetics. For consumers, the combination of citrus intensity and old-school Bubba depth offers more complexity than another straightforward orange strain. Its high THC level means it will not suit every situation or tolerance, yet experienced cannabis enthusiasts looking for potency, resin, distinctive terpene contrast, and an unusual marriage of modern citrus and classic Kush genetics may find Clementine Slush particularly memorable.
